title: Sunflower Seed Kernels, Dry Roasted, with Salt

content.title: About
content.content: Sunflower seed kernels are the edible seeds of the sunflower plant (Helianthus annuus). In the dry‑roasted version they are toasted until golden and then lightly salted. The result is a crunchy snack with a mildly nutty flavor and a salty finish. They are enjoyed on their own or used as an ingredient in cooking and baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sunflower is one of the world’s most widely cultivated oilseed crops.
Dry roasting preserves most nutrients while giving the seeds a richer aroma.
Sunflower seeds are a rich source of vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant.
Historically, sunflower seeds were eaten as food and pressed for oil by indigenous peoples.
Adding salt after roasting enhances flavor perception and makes the snack more appealing.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E protects cells from oxidative damage and supports skin health.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Seeds contain polyunsaturated fatty acids, including linoleic acid, which are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Protein contributes to muscle maintenance, while fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains phytosterols
items.content: Phytosterols may help lower cholesterol levels.

items.title: Seed allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to sunflower seeds.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Excessive salt can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Dry‑roasted seeds are relatively high in calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: Small seeds can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the seeds as a snack, sprinkle them over salads, yogurt, oatmeal, or incorporate them into baked goods. They can also be ground into sunflower seed butter or used in homemade granola.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry‑roasted seeds in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer shelf life keep them refrigerated to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any seeds that develop a rancid smell.
